newsitem.title: USA: CBOT November soy to see minimal to no deliveries.
newsitem.headline: CBOT November soy to see minimal to no deliveries.

text.p: Minimal to zero deliveries were expected to be posted Thursday, first notice day for deliveries on the CBOT Nov soybean contract, traders said.
"Zero, none...no one wants to play that game with the basis as strong as it is and with the strong demand," a trader said.

Exports of U.S. soybeans have been strong with China a recent buyer, and there are indications Brazil is in the market for U.S. soybeans. According to the head of USDA's interagency soybean estimates committee, Brazil could buy up to 500,000 tonnes or more of U.S. soybeans.
Traders also pointed to slow farmer selling of the newly harvested soybean and the firm tone in cash soybean markets as keys to the light delivery scenario.
There is little incentive to deliver soybeans on a roughly $7.00 per bushel contract with the U.S. barge cif basis running at 38 cents per bushel over January, the traders said.
CBOT November soybeans Tuesday closed at $6.98-1/2 and January closed at $6.98-1/4.
As of Tuesday, there were 535,000 bushels of soybeans in Chicago and 65,000 in Toledo registered for possible delivery.
